title: Where the Archive Learns Its Roots Climb Upward

features.name: ascending filament
features.desc-on-touch: A root rendered in diagnostic white rises upward, each hair-thin fiber reaching toward cloud. You follow it with your eye until it dissolves into the pale ground.

features.name: inverted anchor-stone
features.desc-on-touch: What should weigh downward floats instead, a stone reading its own weight as sky. Its corners glow with soft rust.

features.name: codex-stack standing
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard notation: ARCHIVE GROWTH VECTORS / ASCENDING RECORDS / CHECKSUM: ROOTS OUTWEIGHING EARTH. The pages flutter though there is no wind.

features.name: pale burl-node
features.desc-on-touch: A single casing gleams in the cloud—antenna pointing not outward but upward into grey. Its screen reads NODE ASCENDING / SIGNAL REACHING.

inscription: the roots reach upward; the cloud remembers stone; the archive grows in directions the map cannot follow; inversion is not loss

file.name: CloudVector_RootGrowth_DirectionalDrift.txt
file.note: Early readings of upward-reaching archive sensors—nodes responding to cloud as if it were earth, recording sky-bound coordinates. Corruption flag: the archive may have learned growth has no single dir

reverie.title: REVERIE — cloud where the archive forgets its roots
narr: You stand in cloud where tree-trunks fade to outline. Katita
points upward. The roots, she says, are not holding on only.
They climb. They reach where stone could never climb.
The whole forest learns it was built to grow in every direction.
You feel it—the reaching upward. The archive has no bottom here.

exits.label: back down through cloud, where the mountain climbs to meet you
deeper into cloud, where roots become completely weightless
toward a place where sky learned it was also a kind of soil
into mist where the archive forgets which way is holding
